projects.name: Uptime Monitor
projects.summary: Checks your websites and services every few seconds, keeps incident history, and tells you on Discord, Slack, Telegram, a webhook or email when something goes down.
projects.problem: Hosted uptime services charge per monitor and keep your check history on their servers. This one runs as a single process on any small server and stores everything in one SQLite file.
features: HTTP, HTTPS, SSL certificate, TCP, UDP, DNS, Ping, WebSocket, Heartbeat and Domain expiry monitors
DOWN after a configurable number of failures, incident history, 24h / 7d / 30d uptime
Discord, Slack, Telegram, generic JSON webhook and SMTP notifications with per-monitor policy
Public status page with maintenance and incident announcements
Maintenance mode, pause and resume, monitor groups, JSON and CSV export, daily backups
Admin dashboard with password sign-in and optional TOTP two-factor authentication
limitations: Checks run from one location only
WHOIS parsing depends on each registry's response format
Ping monitors need the system ping binary

projects.name: Post Scheduler
projects.summary: Write posts and threads, attach images, schedule them or add them to a daily queue, and publish to Mastodon and Bluesky from one place.
projects.problem: Scheduling tools for social media are subscription products that hold your drafts and your account tokens. This one keeps both on your machine, encrypted, and talks to Mastodon and Bluesky directly.
features: Posts and threads with live character counters per network
Schedule for a time, add to the next free queue slot, save as draft, or publish now
Cross-post to several accounts at once; each network's limits are checked
Up to four images per thread part with alt text
Automatic retries with a delay, then a failed state with the provider's error
Encrypted account tokens, admin sign-in with optional TOTP
limitations: Not yet verified against live accounts by a second person

projects.name: Link Shortener
projects.summary: Short links on your own domain with click statistics by day, referrer, browser and device, without storing anyone's IP address.
projects.problem: Link shorteners sit between your audience and your content and keep the click data. Running your own keeps the domain, the links and the statistics under your control.
features: Generated or custom slugs, titles, expiry dates and click limits
Clicks per day for 30 days, referrers, browsers, operating systems and devices
Unique visitors counted with a daily-rotating hash; IP addresses are never stored
QR code for every link, 302 or cached 301 redirects
API token for creating links from scripts
Admin sign-in with optional TOTP
limitations: Small built-in user-agent heuristic rather than a full parser

projects.name: Booking Page
projects.summary: Define event types and weekly availability, share a link, and let guests pick a free slot in their own time zone. Invitations go out as .ics files and email.
projects.problem: Appointment tools charge per seat and keep your guests' details. This one runs on your server, handles time zones and daylight saving with the built-in Intl API, and keeps bookings in SQLite.
features: Event types with duration, slot step, buffer, minimum notice and booking horizon
Weekly availability windows and blocked time for vacations
Public booking page with calendar and slots shown in the guest's time zone
Double-booking protection at confirmation time
Calendar invitations (.ics), SMTP confirmations and cancellations, guest self-cancellation
Dashboard for event types, bookings and blocked time; admin sign-in with optional TOTP
limitations: No Google or Outlook calendar sync
No rescheduling flow; guests cancel and book again

planned.name: Git-based vault sync
planned.note: An idea, not a promise. It would sync an Obsidian vault through a Git remote you control.

notPlanned.reason: A password manager is security-critical software where a mistake harms people directly, and Vaultwarden already is an excellent, widely audited self-hosted implementation of the Bitwarden API.
